When the panels actually wake

Every observed first and last light across six years, against the fitted window and astronomical sunrise. Weather pushes points inward; the envelope tracks the outer edge.

The model

Solar elevation at each day edge, points coloured by year. Dotted lines are the pooled 5th percentiles, solid lines the 2-harmonic fit. The threshold rises by about a degree in winter, when the inverter needs more irradiance to start. The start-up threshold steps by about 1.2° at the 2023/2024 boundary — larger than the seasonal signal itself, and coincident with the smallest reported power jumping from 1 W to 6 W, so this is a reporting or hardware regime change rather than gradual drift. The pooled fit shown here describes the 2020-2023 regime more than the current one.

Shading screen

A flat line means no obstruction. Read this only as a screen, not a horizon profile — the azimuth bins mix seasons, since morning azimuth 130° is reached both at midwinter sunrise and in summer mid-morning.

The complement of the solar window, in hours.

Data coverage

Generating samples per day. 2020 begins on 20 May, so early day-of-year thresholds draw on five years rather than six.

Geometric solar elevation via pvlib, fitted as a 2-harmonic seasonal threshold on 5th-percentile pooled observations (±10 days).
